question: Compare on-time rate and cost per package for milkrun vs direct, last quarter.
ai_sql:
WITH run_cost AS (
    SELECT run_type, SUM(cost_eur) AS total_cost_eur
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY run_type
),
shipment_stats AS (
    SELECT tr.run_type,
           COUNT(*) AS shipments,
           SUM(s.packages) AS packages,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_to_node_date IS NOT NULL
                     AND s.delivered_to_node_date <= s.promised_date
                    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_shipments
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY tr.run_type
)
SELECT ss.run_type,
       ss.shipments,
       ROUND(100.0 * ss.on_time_shipments / ss.shipments, 1) AS on_time_pct,
       ss.packages,
       ROUND(rc.total_cost_eur, 2) AS total_cost_eur,
       ROUND(rc.total_cost_eur / ss.packages, 2) AS cost_per_package_eur
FROM shipment_stats ss
JOIN run_cost rc ON rc.run_type = ss.run_type
ORDER BY ss.run_type;
assumptions: Last quarter = Q3 2026 (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30), using truck_runs.run_date as the pickup date for both metrics. | On-time rate denominator = all non-cancelled shipments linked to a truck run; shipments with no run_id are excluded because they have no run_type. | On-time = delivered_to_node_date on or before promised_date; undelivered shipments count as not on time. | Cost per package = total cost_eur of all runs of each type in the quarter, including wasted runs, divided by packages of non-cancelled shipments on those runs. | Run cost and shipment packages are aggregated separately before joining to avoid double-counting.
ai_answer: Direct delivery was more reliable, with 87.8% of shipments on time, compared with 72.6% for milkrun. Milkrun was cheaper per package at €2.67, versus €4.88 for direct. This covers Q3 2026 (1 July to 30 September 2026) by truck run pickup date, across 47,300 direct shipments and 23,969 milkrun shipments, excluding cancelled shipments and shipments not linked to a run.

question: What was our weekly attainment for FR shippers last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
fr_days AS (
    SELECT f.shipper_id,
           f.forecast_date,
           f.forecast_packages,
           COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages,
           date(f.forecast_date, '-' || strftime('%w', f.forecast_date) || ' days') AS week_start
    FROM forecasts f
    JOIN shippers sh
      ON sh.shipper_id = f.shipper_id
     AND sh.country = 'FR'
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id
     AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
)
SELECT week_start,
       SUM(actual_packages) AS actual_packages,
       SUM(forecast_packages) AS forecast_packages,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(actual_packages) / SUM(forecast_packages), 1) AS attainment_pct
FROM fr_days
WHERE week_start BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY week_start
ORDER BY week_start;
assumptions: Last quarter = Q3 2026 (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30), per the glossary. | FR shippers are identified by shippers.country = 'FR'; all FR shippers are included regardless of active or de-listed status. | Attainment is aggregated across all FR shippers per week (sum of actual ÷ sum of forecast), not calculated per shipper. | Weeks are Sunday-to-Saturday labelled by week_start. A week counts if its week_start is in Q3, so the week starting 2026-06-28 is excluded and the week starting 2026-09-27 is included in full, including any forecast days on 1–3 October. | Only forecast days count toward attainment; actual volume is matched to forecast_date on the truck run_date, and days with no actual volume count as zero.
ai_answer: Weekly attainment for FR shippers in Q3 2026 ranged from 95.9% (week starting 16 August) to 98.9% (week starting 5 July), and every week fell short of forecast. question: Did any de-listed shipper have volume after being de-listed?

       COUNT(DISTINCT tr.run_date) AS days_with_volume_after,

question: Which nodes went over capacity during peak 2025, and on how many days?

question: Which Account Managers' shippers drove the most avoidable cost last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH run_avoidable AS (
    SELECT tr.run_id,
           CASE WHEN tr.run_outcome = 'wasted' THEN tr.cost_eur ELSE 0 END
         + CASE WHEN tr.is_adhoc = 1 THEN tr.cost_eur * 0.6 / 1.6 ELSE 0 END AS avoidable_eur
    FROM truck_runs tr
    WHERE tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
),
stop_counts AS (
    SELECT run_id, COUNT(*) AS n_stops
    FROM run_stops
    GROUP BY run_id
)
SELECT s.account_manager,
       ROUND(SUM(ra.avoidable_eur / sc.n_stops), 2) AS avoidable_cost_eur
FROM run_avoidable ra
JOIN run_stops rs ON rs.run_id = ra.run_id
JOIN stop_counts sc ON sc.run_id = ra.run_id
JOIN shippers s ON s.shipper_id = rs.shipper_id
GROUP BY s.account_manager
ORDER BY avoidable_cost_eur DESC;
assumptions: Last quarter = Q3 2026 (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30), decided by truck_runs.run_date. | Avoidable cost per run = full cost_eur if run_outcome = 'wasted' plus cost_eur * 0.6 / 1.6 if is_adhoc = 1; a run that is both wasted and ad-hoc contributes both parts. | Each run's avoidable cost is split equally across its run_stops rows, and each share is attributed to that stop's shipper and then to shippers.account_manager (current value). | Runs with no run_stops rows are excluded because they cannot be attributed to any shipper.
ai_answer: Denis Davies's shippers drove the most avoidable cost in Q3 2026 (July 1 to September 30, 2026, by run date), at €21,625.74. question: How much unplanned volume did we get on bank holidays in 2026, by country?
ai_sql:
WITH holiday_2026 AS (
    SELECT country, holiday_date
    FROM holidays
    WHERE holiday_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-12-31'
),
holiday_actual AS (
    -- filter to 2026 holiday dates first, then aggregate shipper x pickup day
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM truck_runs tr
    JOIN holiday_2026 h ON h.holiday_date = tr.run_date
    JOIN shipments s ON s.run_id = tr.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
)
SELECT sh.country,
       SUM(ha.actual_packages) AS unplanned_packages,
       COUNT(*) AS unplanned_shipper_days
FROM holiday_actual ha
JOIN shippers sh
  ON sh.shipper_id = ha.shipper_id
JOIN holiday_2026 h
  ON h.country = sh.country
 AND h.holiday_date = ha.pickup_date
LEFT JOIN forecasts f
  ON f.shipper_id = ha.shipper_id
 AND f.forecast_date = ha.pickup_date
WHERE f.shipper_id IS NULL
GROUP BY sh.country
ORDER BY sh.country;

ai_answer: Unplanned volume on bank holidays in 2026 was 7,326 packages in France, 6,096 in the UK, 5,718 in Italy, and 4,886 in Spain. question: Which shippers missed the +/-10% attainment band for 3+ consecutive weeks?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
daily AS (
    SELECT f.shipper_id, f.forecast_date, f.forecast_packages,
           COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages
    FROM forecasts f
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
),
weekly AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           date(forecast_date, '-' || strftime('%w', forecast_date) || ' days') AS week_start,
           1.0 * SUM(actual_packages) / SUM(forecast_packages) AS attainment
    FROM daily
    GROUP BY shipper_id, week_start
),
missed AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, week_start, attainment
    FROM weekly
    WHERE attainment < 0.9 OR attainment > 1.1
),
islands AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, week_start,
           CAST(julianday(week_start) AS INTEGER)
             - 7 * ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY shipper_id ORDER BY week_start) AS grp
    FROM missed
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, grp, COUNT(*) AS streak_weeks,
           MIN(week_start) AS streak_start, MAX(week_start) AS streak_end
    FROM islands
    GROUP BY shipper_id, grp
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
)
SELECT sh.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       MAX(st.streak_weeks) AS longest_missed_streak_weeks,
       MIN(st.streak_start) AS first_streak_start,
       MAX(st.streak_end) AS last_streak_end
FROM streaks st
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = st.shipper_id
GROUP BY sh.shipper_id, sh.name
ORDER BY longest_missed_streak_weeks DESC, sh.shipper_id;
assumptions: No period was specified, so the check covers all weeks present in the forecasts table. | Weeks run Sunday to Saturday, labelled by week_start; a week's attainment is sum of actual divided by sum of forecast over the days in that week that have forecast rows. | 'Missed the band' means weekly attainment below 90% or above 110%. | Consecutive means consecutive calendar weeks that each have forecast rows; a week with no forecast rows breaks the streak. | The low-volume exclusion (weekly forecast below 50 packages) is not applied, because the question asks which shippers missed the band rather than ranking them by attainment. | Shipper names come from shippers.name; the streak reported is the longest run of consecutive missed weeks per shipper.
ai_answer: **268 shippers** missed the ±10% attainment band (below 90% or above 110%) for at least three consecutive weeks. The check covers every week in the forecasts table, from 29 Dec 2024 to 27 Sep 2026, and excludes cancelled shipments. Twelve shippers, including Fisher Ltd and Cox and Sons, show a streak of 92 weeks, which covers almost the entire period. Those twelve are worth checking for a data or forecasting issue before treating them as performance problems.

question: For milkruns, which shippers are most often the cause of late node arrivals?
ai_sql:
WITH milkrun_stops AS (
    SELECT rs.run_id,
           rs.shipper_id,
           rs.stop_sequence,
           (julianday(rs.actual_pickup_time) - julianday(rs.planned_pickup_time)) * 1440.0 AS lateness_min
    FROM run_stops rs
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = rs.run_id
    WHERE tr.run_type = 'milkrun'
),
stop_delay AS (
    -- delay added by each stop = its lateness minus the previous stop's lateness
    SELECT run_id,
           shipper_id,
           stop_sequence,
           lateness_min - COALESCE(LAG(lateness_min) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY stop_sequence), 0) AS delay_added
    FROM milkrun_stops
),
late_milkruns AS (
    SELECT run_id
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_type = 'milkrun'
      AND run_outcome = 'completed'
      AND actual_arrival_time > planned_arrival_time
),
blamed AS (
    -- blame the stop that added the most delay on each late milkrun
    SELECT sd.run_id,
           sd.shipper_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sd.run_id ORDER BY sd.delay_added DESC, sd.stop_sequence) AS rn
    FROM stop_delay sd
    JOIN late_milkruns lm ON lm.run_id = sd.run_id
),
shipper_milkruns AS (
    SELECT shipper_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT run_id) AS milkruns
    FROM milkrun_stops
    GROUP BY shipper_id
)
SELECT b.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       COUNT(*) AS late_milkruns_blamed,
       sm.milkruns AS total_milkruns,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / sm.milkruns, 1) AS blamed_pct_of_milkruns
FROM blamed b
JOIN shipper_milkruns sm ON sm.shipper_id = b.shipper_id
LEFT JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = b.shipper_id
WHERE b.rn = 1
  AND sm.milkruns >= 20
GROUP BY b.shipper_id, sh.name, sm.milkruns
ORDER BY late_milkruns_blamed DESC;
assumptions: Late milkrun = completed milkrun with actual_arrival_time > planned_arrival_time, over all dates (no period specified). | Stop lateness = (actual_pickup_time - planned_pickup_time) in minutes; the first stop's previous lateness is treated as 0. | Each late milkrun is blamed on the single stop with the largest delay added; ties go to the earlier stop_sequence. | The 20-milkrun minimum is applied to each shipper's total milkruns across all outcomes (not only completed ones). | Shippers with no stop-level pickup times are excluded from the blame count because their lateness cannot be computed.
ai_answer: **Adam 453 is most often the cause of late node arrivals on milkruns, blamed for 185 of its 191 milkruns (96.9%).** Anichini-Zabarella SPA 579 (178 of 183) and Ferrand 496 (171 of 177) follow closely. Nineteen shippers are blamed for more than 80% of their milkruns, and every shipper below them in the list is under 20%. The figures cover all dates, counting only completed milkruns that arrived after their planned time, for shippers with at least 20 milkruns. The list shows only the first 50 of 961 shippers.
